title: Threshold approximation guarantee
statement: Let an algorithm be a polynomial-time map on binary strings, and let an encoded maximization problem have instance language $L$, feasibility relation $F$, objective value $v$, and optimum value $\mathrm{OPT}$. For rational thresholds $a$ and $b$, the algorithm is an $(a,b)$ threshold approximation if, for every $x\in L$, its output is feasible for $x$, and whenever $b\le \mathrm{OPT}(x)$, that output has value at least $a$.
hypotheses_covered: Algorithm is a polynomial-time map on binary strings
Input belongs to the problem’s instance language
Output is feasible for every well-formed input
If the optimum threshold is at most the instance optimum, the output threshold is at most the output value
